commands: . /venv/bin/activate && python -V && pip -V
. /venv/bin/activate && pip3 install tensorflow==1.12.0 > /tmp/tf.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"; tail -n 6 /tmp/tf.log

. /venv/bin/activate && if grep -q 'No matching distribution found for tensorflow==1.12.0' /tmp/tf.log; then echo "VERDICT: pip3 install tensorflow==1.12.0 FAILS on $(python -V 2>&1) (no wheel/sdist for this interpreter)"; else python -c 'import tensorflow as tf; print("VERDICT: installed", tf.__version__)'; fi
. /venv/bin/activate && echo 'Versions pip can see for this interpreter (oldest at the end):' && pip3 index versions tensorflow 2>/dev/null | head -n 2
probes.note: Claim is tested on current Python (the interpreter a fresh reader would have). Expected outcome per hint: resolution failure; tensorflow 1.12.0 only has cp35/cp36 wheels. p-c4 separately tries the install on python:3.6-slim.

setup: apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq gcc libc6-dev >/dev/null
commands: cd /w && python3 -V && pip3 install -r requirements.txt > /tmp/req.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"; grep -iE 'error|failed|Successfully installed' /tmp/req.log | head -n 8

cd /w && for p in fire regex requests tqdm; do spec=$(grep -i "^$p" requirements.txt); pip3 install "$spec" > /tmp/$p.log 2>&1 && echo "OK   $spec" || { echo "FAIL $spec"; grep -iE 'error' /tmp/$p.log | head -n 3; }; done
python3 -c 'import fire, regex, requests, tqdm; print("IMPORT OK", regex.__version__, requests.__version__, tqdm.__version__)' || echo 'IMPORT FAIL'
probes.note: gcc is installed in setup so a failure is attributable to the pins (regex==2017.4.5 is sdist-only and must compile against a 3.11 C-API), not to a missing compiler.

commands: echo "download_model.py 124M exit=$(cat /tmp/dl.exit) (124 = killed by 95s timeout)"; tail -c 300 /tmp/dl.log; echo
echo '--- storage endpoint HEAD checks (all four documented sizes) ---'; cat /tmp/head.txt

cd /w && for f in checkpoint encoder.json hparams.json model.ckpt.data-00000-of-00001 model.ckpt.index model.ckpt.meta vocab.bpe; do test -s models/124M/$f && echo "PRESENT $f $(stat -c %s models/124M/$f)" || echo "MISSING $f"; done
python3 -c 'import json; print("hparams:", json.load(open("/w/models/124M/hparams.json")))' || echo 'hparams.json unreadable'

if [ "$(cat /tmp/dl.exit)" = 0 ]; then echo 'VERDICT: script completed; models/124M populated'; elif [ "$(cat /tmp/dl.exit)" = 124 ]; then echo 'VERDICT: PARTIAL - script runs and endpoint serves files but full 124M (~500MB) did not finish in budget; judge by HEAD statuses + files present'; else echo 'VERDICT: script errored'; fi
probes.note: The 124M checkpoint is ~500MB; the probe budget may cut the transfer. HEAD checks on all four sizes settle 'endpoint still serves' independent of bandwidth.

setup: apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq gcc libc6-dev >/dev/null
pip3 install tensorflow==1.12.0 > /tmp/tf36.log 2>&1; echo "TF_INSTALL_EXIT=$?" | tee /tmp/tf36.exit; tail -n 2 /tmp/tf36.log
cd /w && pip3 install -r requirements.txt > /tmp/req36.log 2>&1; echo "REQ_INSTALL_EXIT=$?" | tee /tmp/req36.exit
commands: cat /tmp/tf36.exit /tmp/req36.exit; echo "download exit=$(cat /tmp/dl.exit)"; python3 -c 'import tensorflow as tf; print("tensorflow", tf.__version__)' || echo 'TF IMPORT FAIL'
cd /w && ls models/124M 2>/dev/null | wc -l | xargs -I{} echo 'model files present: {}/7'

cd /w && export PYTHONIOENCODING=UTF-8 && timeout 60 python3 src/generate_unconditional_samples.py | tee /tmp/samples > /dev/null 2>/tmp/gen.err; echo "EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]} (124 expected: default nsamples=0 means generate forever)"

grep -n 'nsamples=0' /w/src/generate_unconditional_samples.py; grep -c 'SAMPLE 1 ' /tmp/samples | xargs -I{} echo 'SAMPLE-1 headers in /tmp/samples: {}'; head -c 600 /tmp/samples; echo; tail -n 3 /tmp/gen.err

if grep -q 'SAMPLE 1 ' /tmp/samples; then echo 'VERDICT: documented command emits text samples (terminated by probe timeout, not by the script)'; else echo 'VERDICT: no samples produced - see gen.err and gating exits above'; fi
probes.note: Only image where tensorflow==1.12.0 has a wheel is a 3.5/3.6 interpreter, so python:3.6-slim is used. TF install + 500MB model + CPU sampling will likely exceed 120s; the probe records which gate broke. The verbatim command never terminates by design (nsamples default 0) - that is itself a finding.

cd /w && pip3 install -r requirements.txt > /tmp/req36.log 2>&1; echo "REQ_INSTALL_EXIT=$?" | tee /tmp/req36.exit

cd /w && python3 src/interactive_conditional_samples.py --help 2>&1 | grep -iE 'top_k|length|nsamples' | head -n 5 || echo 'CLI --help failed'

cd /w && export PYTHONIOENCODING=UTF-8 && printf 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog because\n' | timeout 60 python3 src/interactive_conditional_samples.py --top_k 40 --length 20 > /tmp/cond 2>/tmp/cond.err; echo "EXIT=$? (EOFError after the first sample is expected: script loops on input() and stdin is exhausted)"
grep -c 'SAMPLE 1 ' /tmp/cond | xargs -I{} echo 'SAMPLE-1 headers: {}'; head -c 500 /tmp/cond; echo; grep -E 'EOFError|Error' /tmp/cond.err | tail -n 2

if grep -q 'SAMPLE 1 ' /tmp/cond; then echo 'VERDICT: prompt in, model continuation out via --top_k 40 (--length 20 added only to fit time budget)'; else echo 'VERDICT: no conditional sample produced - see gating exits'; fi
probes.note: Same environment gate as p-c4. --length 20 is a deviation from the verbatim command (default length = full 1024-token context, too slow on CPU in budget); it does not change the interface being tested.

setup:
python3 -c 'import re,urllib.request,json
for f in ["Dockerfile.cpu","Dockerfile.gpu"]:
    base=re.search(r"^FROM\\s+(\\S+)",open("/w/"+f).read(),re.M).group(1); repo,tag=base.split(":")
    if "/" not in repo: repo="library/"+repo
    url="https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/%s/tags/%s"%(repo,tag)
    try:
        d=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url,headers={"User-Agent":"probe"}))); print(f,base,"HUB_TAG_OK last_updated=",d.get("last_updated"),"full_size=",d.get("full_size"))
    except Exception as e: print(f,base,"HUB_TAG_ERR",e)' > /tmp/hub.txt 2>&1
commands: cd /w && ls -la Dockerfile.cpu Dockerfile.gpu && echo '--- Dockerfile.cpu ---' && cat Dockerfile.cpu && echo '--- Dockerfile.gpu ---' && cat Dockerfile.gpu
echo '--- Docker Hub tag existence for each FROM base ---'; cat /tmp/hub.txt

command -v docker >/dev/null && echo 'docker present' || echo 'docker: not available inside probe container - `docker build` NOT attempted; verdict rests on Dockerfile presence + base-tag availability'

if grep -q 'Dockerfile.cpu.*HUB_TAG_OK' /tmp/hub.txt; then echo 'VERDICT: CPU base image tag still resolvable on Docker Hub; build path plausible but unexecuted'; else echo 'VERDICT: CPU base tag NOT resolvable - documented build cannot start'; fi
probes.note: A python container cannot run docker build; this probe settles the pre-condition (files exist, base tags still pull). Full build belongs in the GitHub Actions execution arm.

commands: python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open("/tmp/repo.json")); print("archived=",d["archived"],"pushed_at=",d["pushed_at"],"default_branch=",d["default_branch"],"open_issues=",d["open_issues_count"])'

python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(open("/tmp/repo.json")); assert d["archived"] is True, "repo is NOT archived on GitHub"; print("VERDICT: GitHub reports archived=true, matching README Status: Archive")'

setup:
python3 -c 'import urllib.request
r=urllib.request.Request("https://api.github.com/repos/openai/gpt-2/contents/model_card.md?ref=9b63575ef42771a015060c964af2c3da4cf7c8ab",headers={"User-Agent":"probe"})
try:
    resp=urllib.request.urlopen(r); open("/tmp/mc_status","w").write(str(resp.status))
except Exception as e: open("/tmp/mc_status","w").write("ERR "+str(e))'
commands: echo "GitHub contents API status for model_card.md@pinned SHA: $(cat /tmp/mc_status)"
test -f /w/model_card.md && echo 'model_card.md PRESENT in pinned tree' && wc -lc /w/model_card.md && head -n 12 /w/model_card.md || echo 'model_card.md MISSING in pinned tree'
grep -n 'model_card.md' /w/README.md

grep -qiE 'model (details|description|type)|intended use|training data' /w/model_card.md && echo 'VERDICT: model card present and contains basic model info sections' || echo 'VERDICT: file exists but lacks recognizable model-card sections'
grep -n -iE '117M|345M|parameter counts were wrong' /w/README.md
echo '--- model names used by code/docs ---'; grep -n -E '124M|355M|117M|345M' /w/DEVELOPERS.md /w/download_model.py /w/Dockerfile.cpu /w/Dockerfile.gpu | head -n 20
echo '--- download_model.py: how model name is taken (no whitelist => any name is passed to the URL) ---'; grep -n -E 'sys.argv|model = |models/' /w/download_model.py
echo '--- storage endpoint: which names actually exist ---'; cat /tmp/hp_status.txt

python3 -c 'import json
for m in ["124M","355M"]:
    h=json.load(open("/tmp/hp_"+m+".json")); e=h["n_embd"]; L=h["n_layer"]
    p=h["n_vocab"]*e+h["n_ctx"]*e+2*e+L*(12*e*e+13*e)
    print(m,h,"computed_params=%.1fM"%(p/1e6))
    assert abs(p/1e6-float(m[:-1]))<1.0, "name does not match computed size"
print("VERDICT: 124M/355M names match parameter counts computed from hparams (wte+wpe+ln_f+L*(12d^2+13d))")' || echo 'VERDICT: could not confirm - see hp_status'
grep -n -B3 -A4 'PYTHONIOENCODING' /w/DEVELOPERS.md /w/README.md || echo 'PYTHONIOENCODING not documented in DEVELOPERS.md/README.md'

python3 -V; echo '--- case A: C locale, no var, modern defaults (PEP 538/540 locale coercion) ---'; env -i LANG=C /usr/local/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; print("stdout.encoding=",sys.stdout.encoding); print("\u00e9\u2014\u4e2d")' && echo 'A: no UnicodeEncodeError without the variable' || echo 'A: UnicodeEncodeError without the variable'

echo '--- case B: C locale, coercion+utf8 mode disabled (legacy 3.6-era behaviour) ---'; env -i LANG=C PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 PYTHONUTF8=0 /usr/local/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; print("stdout.encoding=",sys.stdout.encoding); print("\u00e9\u2014\u4e2d")' && echo 'B: no error even in legacy mode' || echo 'B: UnicodeEncodeError - this is the failure the documented variable addresses'

echo '--- case C: same legacy mode + PYTHONIOENCODING=UTF-8 (the documented fix) ---'; env -i LANG=C PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONIOENCODING=UTF-8 /usr/local/bin/python3 -c 'import sys; print("stdout.encoding=",sys.stdout.encoding); print("\u00e9\u2014\u4e2d")' && echo 'C: variable forces UTF-8 stdout, no error' || echo 'C: STILL fails with the variable set'
echo 'VERDICT: documented instruction is real and effective (case C); whether it is REQUIRED depends on interpreter era - compare A vs B above'
